arxiv-2102-13479.title: Towards Explaining Expressive Qualities in Piano Recordings: Transfer of Explanatory Features via Acoustic Domain Adaptation
arxiv-2102-13479.creator: Shreyan Chowdhury Gerhard Widmer
arxiv-2102-13479.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Shreyan Chowdhury Gerhard Widmer. Emotion and expressivity in music have been topics of considerable interest in the field of music information retrieval. In recent years, mid-level perceptual features have been suggested as means to explain computational predictions of musical emotion. We find that the diversity of musical styles and genres in the available dataset for learning these features is not sufficient for models to generalise well to specialised acoustic domains such as solo piano music.

arxiv-2105-01097.title: Illuminating entanglement shadows of BTZ black holes by a generalized entanglement measure
arxiv-2105-01097.creator: Marius Gerbershagen
arxiv-2105-01097.description: Abstract We define a generalized entanglement measure in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence. Compared to the ordinary entanglement entropy for a spatial subregion dual to the area of the Ryu-Takayanagi surface, we take into account both entanglement between spatial degrees of freedom as well as between different fields of the boundary theory.

arxiv-2401-06563.title: Resource-Efficient Gesture Recognition using Low-Resolution Thermal Camera via Spiking Neural Networks and Sparse Segmentation
arxiv-2401-06563.creator: Ali Safa, Wout Mommen and Lars Keuninckx imec, Leuven, Belgium, ESAT, KU Leuven, Belgium, ETRO, VUB, Brussels, Belgium
arxiv-2401-06563.description: Abstract This work proposes a novel approach for hand gesture recognition using an inexpensive, low-resolution ( 24 × 32 24\times 32 ) thermal sensor processed by a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) followed by Sparse Segmentation and feature-based gesture classification via Robust Principal Component Analysis (R-PCA).

arxiv-2406-17768.title: EXTRACT: Efficient Policy Learning by Extracting Transferable Robot Skills from Offline Data
arxiv-2406-17768.creator: Jesse Zhang, Minho Heo, Zuxin Liu, Erdem Bıyık, Joseph J. Lim, Yao Liu, Rasool Fakoor
arxiv-2406-17768.description: Abstract Most reinforcement learning (RL) methods focus on learning optimal policies over low-level action spaces. While these methods can perform well in their training environments, they struggle with learning new tasks. Instead, RL agents acting over useful, temporally extended skills rather than low-level actions can learn new tasks more easily.

arxiv-2407-01054.title: Joint Pruning and Channel-wise Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2407-01054.creator: Beatrice Alessandra Motetti, Matteo Risso, Alessio Burrello, Enrico Macii, Massimo Poncino, and Daniele Jahier Pagliari
arxiv-2407-01054.description: Abstract The resource requirements of deep neural networks (DNNs) pose significant challenges to their deployment on edge devices. Common approaches to address this issue are pruning and mixed-precision quantization, which lead to latency and memory occupation improvements. These optimization techniques are usually applied independently.

arxiv-2410-22417.title: Hybrid quantum-classical approach for combinatorial problems at hadron colliders
arxiv-2410-22417.creator: Zhongtian Dong 1,2, Taejoon Kim 3, Kyoungchul Kong 2, Myeonghun Park 4,5,6, Jacob L. Scott 2, Heechan Yi 7, Willie Aboumrad, Ananth Kaushik, Martin Roetteler
arxiv-2410-22417.description: Abstract In recent years, quantum computing has drawn significant interest within the field of high-energy physics. We explore the potential of quantum algorithms to resolve the combinatorial problems in particle physics experiments. As a concrete example, we consider top quark pair production in the fully hadronic channel at the Large Hadron Collider.

arxiv-2502-08839.title: Assessing Quantum Layout Synthesis Tools via Known Optimal-SWAP Cost Benchmarks
arxiv-2502-08839.creator: Shuohao Ping, Wan-Hsuan Lin, Daniel Bochen Tan, Jason Cong
arxiv-2502-08839.description: Abstract Quantum layout synthesis (QLS) is a critical step in quantum program compilation for superconducting quantum computers, involving the insertion of SWAP gates to satisfy hardware connectivity constraints. While previous works have introduced SWAP-free benchmarks with known-optimal depths for evaluating QLS tools, these benchmarks overlook SWAP count—a key performance metric.

arxiv-2509-04902.title: Coexisting Kagome and Heavy Fermion Flat Bands in YbCr 6 Ge 6
arxiv-2509-04902.creator: Hanoh Lee 1,∗ , Churlhi Lyi 1,∗ , Taehee Lee 1 , Hyeonhui Na 1 , Jinyoung Kim 2 , Sangjae Lee 3 , Younsik Kim 2 , Anil Rajapitamahuni 4 , Asish K. Kundu 4 , Elio Vescovo 4 , Byeong-Gyu Park 5 , Changyoung Kim 2 , Charles H. Ahn 3,6 , Frederick J. Walker 3 , Ji Seop Oh 7,8 , Bo Gyu Jang 9 , ✉ {}^{9,{
arxiv-2509-04902.description: Abstract Abstract Flat bands, emergent in strongly correlated electron systems, stand at the frontier of condensed matter physics, providing fertile ground for unconventional quantum phases. Recent observations of dispersionless bands at the Fermi level in kagome lattice open the possibility of unifying the disjoint paradigms of topology and correlation-driven heavy fermion liquids.

arxiv-2511-14294.title: Uncertainty assessment of spatial dynamic microsimulations
arxiv-2511-14294.creator: Morgane Dumont, Ahmed Alsaloum, Julian Ernst, Jan Weymeirsch, Ralf Münnich, [0.5em] HEC Liege - Management School of the University of Liège
arxiv-2511-14294.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Morgane Dumont, Ahmed Alsaloum, Julian Ernst, Jan Weymeirsch, Ralf Münnich, [0.5em] HEC Liege - Management School of the University of Liège. Spatial dynamic microsimulations probabilistically project geographically referenced units with individual characteristics over time. Like any projection method, their outcomes are inherently uncertain and sensitive to multiple factors. However, such factors are rarely addressed.

arxiv-2601-23249.title: Theoretical Challenges in Learning for Branch-and-Cut
arxiv-2601-23249.creator: Hongyu Cheng, Amitabh Basu
arxiv-2601-23249.description: Abstract Machine learning is increasingly used to guide branch-and-cut (B&C) for mixed-integer linear programming by learning score-based policies for selecting branching variables and cutting planes. Many approaches train on local signals from lookahead heuristics such as strong branching, and linear programming (LP) bound improvement for cut selection. Training and evaluation of the learned models often focus on local score accuracy.

pmc-10605734.creator: İvo Gökmen, Ebru Taştekin, Nazan Demir, Erkan Özcan, Fahri Akgül, Muhammed Bekir Hacıoğlu, Bülent Erdoğan, Sernaz Topaloğlu, İrfan Çiçin
pmc-10605734.description: The aim of our study was to evaluate the incidence of KRAS/NRAS and BRAF mutations, analyze molecular patterns, and investigate associations with clinical parameters of these mutations in CRC KRAS/NRAS and BRAF mutations analyzed by next-generation sequencing. The detection rates of these mutations and patients’ demographics were recorded and the relationship between them was evaluated using the chi-square test.

pmc-10798371.title: Research on Rotating Machinery Fault Diagnosis Based on an Improved Eulerian Video Motion Magnification
pmc-10798371.creator: Haifeng Zhao, Xiaorui Zhang, Dengpan Jiang, Jin Gu, Ramesh K Agarwal
pmc-10798371.description: Rotating machinery condition monitoring and fault diagnosis are important bases for maintenance decisions, as the vibrations generated during operation are usually imperceptible to the naked eye. Eulerian video motion magnification (EVMM) can reveal subtle changes and has been widely used in various fields such as medicine, structural analysis, and fault diagnosis, etc.

pmc-11453349.title: 8452 Paraganglioma Masquerading as Neurological Symptoms: A Rare Case Presentation
pmc-11453349.creator: Arjun Basnet, Sapna Sharma, Madhav Acharya, Sijan Basnet, Kelly Brenan-Rothschild, Chheki Sherpa
pmc-11453349.description: Disclosure: A. Basnet: None. S. Sharma: None. M. Acharya: None. S. Basnet: None. K. Brenan-Rothschild: None. C. Sherpa: None. Introduction: Paragangliomas (PG) are rare tumors of neural crest origin. We report an unusual case of a PG wherein the patient presented to the hospital with complaints of bilateral numbness, tingling, and intermittent difficulty in grasping objects.

pmc-11862499.creator: M Moalla, N Charfi, S Sellami, I Gassara, R Feki, N Smaoui, S Omri, L Zouari, J Ben Thabet, M Maalej Bouali, M Maalej

This community is exposed to sociocultural and legal contexts different from those in Tunisia and the degree of acculturation would tend to increase over time. However, data on the use of psychoactive substances, particularly cannabis, in this particular population are scarce.

pmc-12495506.title: Examining the Gaze Behaviour and Decision‐Making of Field Hockey Players In Situ
pmc-12495506.creator: Bente M. van Dijk, Joris J. A. A. M. Hoeboer, Margot van Wermeskerken, Arie‐Willem de Leeuw, Sanne I. de Vries, David L. Mann
pmc-12495506.description: Gaze behaviour is associated with decision‐making in team sports. For instance, the final fixation of basketball players typically reflects the decision they make. However, it is not clear how athletes adapt in invasive team sports where they also control the ball using an implement (e.g., field hockey or lacrosse).

pmc-12610824.title: Solvent Annealing Influence of PEDOT on Its Electrochemical and Electrochromic Properties
pmc-12610824.creator: Kaiwen Lin, Yuying Jiang, Qinran Chen, Wangdaiqi Kong, Ruiyu Luo, Qianhui Zhou, Hao Liu
pmc-12610824.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The study of effect of solvent annealing on the optoelectronic properties of polymers is not new research hotspot, but the influence of solvent annealing on the electrochemical and electrochromic properties of PEDOT remains unexplored. This paper investigates the effects of three different solvents—chlorobenzene (CB), tetrahydrofuran (THF), and dimethylformamide (DMF)—on the self-assembly of PEDOT films and compares their thermal, morphological, electrochemical, and electrochromic properties.

pmc-12752641.title: RELA Ablation Contributes to Progression of Hepatocellular Carcinoma with TP53R249S Mutation and is a Potential Therapeutic Target
pmc-12752641.creator: Zhiping Wu, Zhe Wang, Diwei Zheng, Yongfang Zheng, Zhiwu Jiang, Jiang Lv, Yueqin Zhu, Heng Jia, Ziyuan Duan, Tingjie Yuan, Qiting Wu, Youguo Long, Shouheng Lin, Yao Yao, Georgia Carson, Jean P Thiery, Kwan Man, Peng Li
pmc-12752641.description: TP53 mutations are highly associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a common and deadly cancer. However, few primary drivers in the progression of HCC with mutant TP53 have been identified. To uncover tumor suppressors in human HCC, a genome‐wide CRISPR/Cas9‐based screening of primary human hepatocytes with MYC and TP53R249S overexpression (MT‐PHHs) is performed in xenografts.

pmc-13057189.title: Ant colony optimization approach for sustainable end-milling with minimum quantity nano-green lubrication
pmc-13057189.creator: Mustafa Abdullah, A C Umamaheshwer Rao, T Ramachandran, Swetarani Biswal, Shivam P Chaudhary, Ripendeep Singh, Akanksha Mishra, Vikasdeep Singh Mann, Abhijit Bhowmik, Yalew Tamene
pmc-13057189.description: With the emergence of environmentally conscious production requirements, machining industries increasingly employ sustainable lubrication strategies to minimize the drawbacks associated with conventional flood cooling. Minimum quantity lubrication (MQL), in which a fine mist of lubricant is directed into the tool–workpiece interface, has gained significant traction owing to its ability to reduce fluid consumption while delivering enhanced lubrication.

pmc-13087816.title: Clinical Outcomes in Bacillus Calmette-Guérin–Exposed Non–Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
pmc-13087816.creator: Maria Giatsoglou, Dimitrios Chatzistavrou, Joan Mazzarelli Sopczynski, Gang Feng, Roger Li
pmc-13087816.description: Key PointsQuestionWhat are the actual burdens and clinical outcomes experienced by individuals with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)–exposed non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC)?FindingsIn this cohort study of 26 876 patients, those with BCG-exposed NMIBC represented a large, underserved population with recurrence occurring in 83%, accounting for more than 80% of disease progression and cystectomy cases.

pmc-13283443.title: Human dignity, technology, and solidarity in a fractured world: why Magnifica Humanitas matters for public health
pmc-13283443.creator: Tiago Correia, Walter Ricciardi, Martin McKee
pmc-13283443.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The encyclical appears at a time when the moral language of public life has become dangerously thin. War, forced displacement, climate insecurity, widening inequality, and weakening multilateral institutions have made solidarity harder to sustain. At the same time, artificial intelligence, digital surveillance, and the concentration of technological power are changing how decisions are made, who is heard, and who is rendered invisible. These are not peripheral concerns for public health. They are among its central questions.

pmc-13363864.title: DualCDM: Dual-Domain Conditional Diffusion for SAR-to-Optical Translation with Spatial–Frequency Correlation and Adaptive Feature Recalibration
pmc-13363864.creator: Yaobin Ma, Hossein Aghababaei, Ling Chang, Jingbo Wei
pmc-13363864.description: Translating Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images into optical images is intrinsically ill-posed because microwave backscatter and optical reflectance describe different physical properties of the observed scene. Although frequency-domain modeling has been introduced into diffusion-based translation, existing methods mainly rely on independent weighting of individual Fourier coefficients and provide limited modeling of interactions among neighboring frequencies and feature channels.

pmc-13392424.title: Timed secreted proteomes reveal regulation of hepatokines by the liver circadian clock
pmc-13392424.creator: Christopher Litwin, Qing Zhang, Ioannis Tsialtas, Zhihong Li, Sophia Hernandez, Steffi Prem, Kristi Dietert, Mallory Keating, Tomoki Sato, Jiyoon Ryu, Lily Q. Dong, Kevin F. Bieniek, Kevin B. Koronowski
pmc-13392424.description: Here, we use an ex vivo approach compatible with the circadian timescale to interrogate protein secretion from liver, revealing several findings. Proteomic analyses in male and female mice identify hundreds of proteins that exhibit time-of-day-dependent or clock-dependent secretion involved in extracellular matrix, immune, redox, xenobiotic, and fatty acid functions.

pmc-13562425.title: Camera-based respiratory rate monitoring in unmodified neonatal intensive care – a cross-sectional study in a UK hospital
pmc-13562425.creator: Alex Grafton, Lynn Thomson, Kathryn Beardsall, Joan Lasenby
pmc-13562425.description: SummaryBackgroundCamera-based methods have shown potential for respiratory rate measurement in neonatal intensive care. However existing work is tested on short recordings, which do not represent the range of environments present in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) or assess challenging conditions such as movement or poor visibility.

pmc-13589079.title: Artificial intelligence in clinical trials—state of the evidence, gaps, and next steps
pmc-13589079.creator: Antonis A. Armoundas, Constantine Tarabanis, Joseph Loscalzo
pmc-13589079.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryArtificial intelligence (AI) affects clinical trials in two distinct but overlapping ways: as the intervention under evaluation and as infrastructure supporting trial design, recruitment, monitoring, endpoint assessment, analysis, and reporting. In this manuscript, we define AI-as-intervention as AI whose output is itself part of the assigned clinical intervention being evaluated for its effect on participant care or outcomes, and AI-for-trial-operations as AI used to support trial design, conduct, or analysis without itself constituting the treatment under study.
